column1: # Which of the entity's two flight models is actually driven.
# THE QUESTION CYCLE 1379 ANSWERED TOO FAST. It concluded "the class this
# campaign ported is genuinely a class that flies" because 0x8200F270 has a
# non-empty slot 11 while the sibling branch overrides it with the empty blr.
# That is an argument about the CLASS. It says nothing about whether the
# INSTANCE is ever reached, and cycle 1384 finds it is not.
# MEASUREMENT 1 -- nothing addresses the +2224 subobject after construction.
# A search over the whole corpus for any register that ever equals `base + 2224`,
# following addi CHAINS from any base register rather than single displacements
# off r3, returns exactly three sites:
#   0x8222BF94  sub_8222BEC8   the constructor
#   0x82227BE4  sub_82227B08   the destructor
#   0x821F5AE4  sub_821F5AD8   a STRING address, 0x820008B0, not a displacement
# No store of that value exists either: the entity's only flight-model pointer is
# +4912, written twice in the whole corpus, both times in a constructor, and both
# times with the OTHER object.
# MEASUREMENT 2 -- the +4912 object is driven, through three of its own slots.
# Dataflow from `lwz rX,4912(rY)` to a virtual dispatch:
# slot
# AND THE ENTITY IS NOT A FLIGHT MODEL ITSELF. Its vtable 0x82007A10 runs to 89
# slots and shares ZERO of 36 with the flight-model base, so there is no
# inheritance path by which slot 11 could reach the model through the entity.
# THE CONCLUSION. For this entity, the live flight model is the 0x8200F310
# branch, stepped through slot 15. The 0x8200F270 instance at +2224 is
# constructed, destructed, and never addressed.
# WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN.
#   The four contracted behaviours -- retail_flight_controls (0x82302DB0),
#   retail_flight_step (0x82303110), retail_flight_orientation (0x82302C88) and
#   retail_flight_step_driver (0x82283898) -- are faithful ports of real retail
#   functions, each verified against the executed instructions. NOTHING here
#   touches that, and their contract statements remain true as written.
#   What is now open is their RELEVANCE. They are 0x8200F270's implementations,
#   and the live model uses 0x8200F310's: slots 30, 31 and 32 are 0x82303E68,
#   0x823042D0 and 0x82306038, and the step is 0x82306A38 -- all different
#   functions, none ported.
# NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the question that now matters more than any of the
# above: whether the player's aircraft is this entity at all. The 10,672-byte
# object of sub_8222BEC8 comes from the factory sub_820A8138 on type ids 1..4,
# and which id the player gets has never been read.
